The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f9b421716dd79df6c7c3a34bbd5a3a9f425e84f4` → `packageMentionDocs`.

This run read `content/docs` from `8351f1e37ccb28c54a75b4e3c4c69dbcc468fa87` — the merge of head `55bb8619e73ad18a8a08a776e7bdee92bca25d03` into base `f9b421716dd79df6c7c3a34bbd5a3a9f425e84f4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8351f1e37ccb28c54a75b4e3c4c69dbcc468fa87 && git checkout 8351f1e37ccb28c54a75b4e3c4c69dbcc468fa87
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f9b421716dd79df6c7c3a34bbd5a3a9f425e84f4 55bb8619e73ad18a8a08a776e7bdee92bca25d03 && git checkout -B drift-repro f9b421716dd79df6c7c3a34bbd5a3a9f425e84f4 && git merge --no-ff 55bb8619e73ad18a8a08a776e7bdee92bca25d03

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f9b421716dd79df6c7c3a34bbd5a3a9f425e84f4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `55bb8619e73ad18a8a08a776e7bdee92bca25d03`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Face: a narrowing of the metadata save door's accept set for `object` (ADR-0029 D9.9). Read from the net diff of the head against `main` at merge-base `394f65e89` (5 files, 359 added, 23 removed; the GitHub diff and a local merge-base diff are byte-equal), card #23416 with every comment but the dispatching seat's own conclusions, and the PR body.

1. `classifyObjectContribution`'s runtime-owner arm — right.
   - Keying: `getObjectOwner(fqn)` reads `objectContributors.get(fqn)` directly, and `registerObject` keys a contributor on `computeFQN(namespace, schema.name)`, which is identity (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`, `computeFQN` returns the short name). Both seams that register a `sys_metadata` object row (`applyObjectRegistryMutation` and `loadMetaFromDb`) pass `namespace` undefined, so the owner the arm reads sits under the same key the registration it predicts would use. The arm predicts the registry's own ADR-0029 D3 refusal exactly: `registerObject` throws `ObjectOwnershipConflictError` when the sitting `own` contributor's `packageId` differs from the incoming one and the late-install branch does not fire (both bodies carry `_provenance: 'org'`), which is `binding !== runtimeOwnerPackageId`. The classifier is asked with `request.name` and the registration carries `item.name`, the same pairing the packaged-owner arm has carried since D9.8; nothing new there.
   - Exclusions, each right: (a) an owner keyed `'sys_metadata'` (a package-less runtime object) is left to today's verdict, because the prescription would name the sentinel as a package; escalated (③.7). (b) an empty binding: at the save door a publish save naming no package is re-addressed by `packagelessAddress` to the one bound row before the classifier runs (the `request.packageId == null`, `source === undefined`, `writeFace !== 'package-duplicate'` block), several bindings are refused as ambiguous, a draft save's binding is resolved by the repository and a draft never registers, and the server-stated rewrites pass `null` only for a package-unbound row; so no `own` verdict on an empty binding reaches `registerObject` against a foreign owner. (c) the owner's own package: `own`, the same-package re-registration branch, pinned by a control. (d) an owner with no `packageId` at all (a bare programmatic `registerObject(schema)`) is also left to today's verdict; it is not a `sys_metadata` shape, since both hydration seams always bind a string, and the docblock says so.
   - Reusing the D9.9 refusal: one arm, the existing code `OBJECT_OVERLAY_PACKAGE_MISMATCH`, status 422, the existing sentence; `ownerPackageId` names the runtime owner's package, so "bind the customization to 'P'" reads correctly to a runtime author. The second remedy, "have 'Q' extend the object", names a code-package affordance; a wording debt of the ruled text, not of this PR (③.9).

2. The three callers — each as the changeset states.
   - Save door (`saveMetaItem`): the classifier runs after `packagelessAddress` and before `ensureOverlayIndex()` and `repo.put`, the method's first writes, so the 422 lands before any row and any history entry. Pinned on a real kernel (no `sys_metadata` or `sys_metadata_history` row for Q; registry and store still say P).
   - Write-through (`applyObjectRegistryMutation`): a `mismatch` throws `overlayPackageMismatchError` into the existing best-effort `console.warn`. Unreachable from `saveMetaItem`, which refuses upstream; reachable from rollback and draft promotion, where the registry's own refusal landed in the same warn before. A log line only.
   - Boot hydration (`loadMetaFromDb`): a `mismatch` throws into the per-record catch, is counted in `errors`, and the first-hydrated row stays registered, as before; the `Failed to hydrate` warn now carries `code=OBJECT_OVERLAY_PACKAGE_MISMATCH` in place of `OBJECT_OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT`. Stated in the changeset.

3. `duplicatePackage`, `copied` to `failed[]` — correct, and at least not worse. The copy's `saveMetaItem` call sits in the catch that pushes `failed[]` with the declared refusal text, and the receipt's `success` holds only when `failed` is empty and `copied` is not. Before this PR a same-name copy (a source object whose name lacks the source namespace prefix) was listed in `copied` with a Q-bound row the registry refused over the same physical table, the D9.9 disagreement under a success receipt. Reporting the failure is the right direction (Prime Directive #10, absence must be loud). The prescription's fit for the duplicate face is #23511, not this PR.

4. The two re-seeded fixtures — real setup changes, assertions untouched.
   - `packages/objectql/src/protocol-delete-object-registry-heal.test.ts`, `twoPackageObject`: the first package's row is still saved through the door; the second is written into the store as the first row's own shape, rebound and re-labelled, with the repository's checksum (`hashSpec`, proved on the row the door just wrote) under a distinct `rowKey` (the key includes `package_id`). The fixture now also asserts the registry holds the first package. Every delete and heal assertion below it is unchanged, and both orders still measure the heal.
   - `packages/rest/src/meta-delete-drop-storage-other-rows.test.ts`: `seedUnboundRow` is generalised to `seedStoredRow(packageId)`, the same direct `engine.insert('sys_metadata', …)` with `seedUnboundRow` kept as its `null` case; `twoPackageObject` saves P through the door and seeds Q. The registry state equals what the refused write-through left (P), and every `[#23415]` assertion is untouched.

5. New pin `packages/objectql/src/protocol-runtime-owner-overlay-refusal.test.ts`: a real `ObjectKernel` with `ObjectQLPlugin` and a memory driver; the refusal (code, status, `packageId`, `ownerPackageId`, no row, no history, registry and store agree on P) and three controls (the owner's re-save answers success and the registry follows; a package-less save is addressed to P's row; a code-packaged owner still answers `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` / 403). `@objectstack/metadata-core` (`hashSpec`) is a declared dependency of `@objectstack/objectql`.

6. Public surface: `classifyObjectContribution` is private; no export, spec key or stored shape moves; every type except `object` is untouched (the classifier runs only for `singularType === 'object'`). No governed path in the file list.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` `minor`, carrying `**BREAKING**`, a `!` summary and `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — right. A narrowing of a published door's accept set is breaking, and `minor` is the launch-window level (`check-changeset-no-major`). No other published package changes: the other four files are tests and the changeset.
- ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — right on substance. No spec key, authorable spelling, export or stored shape is added, removed, renamed or re-shaped, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite; the remedy is on the request a caller sends. A Q-bound row stored before this change was never held by the registry and was already counted in boot `errors`; its exit is an ordinary delete, not a conversion. The body's FROM … TO … bullets describe a request and response behaviour change, a consumer-facing reading, not a prescription for the metadata upgrader, the distinction ADR-0087 itself draws for this category. The dev's first spelling, a FROM → TO section label, was refused by the gate's label convention and rewritten into bullets; the substance of the claim did not move, and the gate passes at the head.
- `Clause-②: no` — right. The card widens no accept set and no public face. The PR body carries `no` with no arm; the changeset carries `no (narrowing)`, which is where `check-adr-0087-registration` reads the breaking signal. The arm is optional on the body line and the two values agree; no contradiction.
- FROM … TO bullets and the remedy — right and complete for the three faces that move (publish save, draft save, `duplicatePackage`), with the unchanged cases stated (the owner's re-save, a package-less save, a code-shipped owner, every other type). The one-line remedy (`?package=P`, no package, or a distinct name; `DELETE …?package=Q` for a leftover row) is what an upgrading agent needs after the 422.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report `6171892674`, each deviation and finding answered or escalated:

1. Surface increment, `packages/rest/src/meta-delete-drop-storage-other-rows.test.ts`, outside claim `6168029604`'s declared surface: accepted. It landed with PR #23464 after the claim, it saves Q through the door, and this PR reds it without the re-seed; a consumer-radius sweep, fixture-only, declared in the PR body.
2. Three callers of the classifier, not two: verified in ①.2; none needed an edit.
3. The FROM → TO label against `check-adr-0087-registration`: answered in ②.
4. Two `origin/main` merges before opening: the net diff against the merge base is the five files and nothing else.
5. Probe tests created and deleted, ablations never committed: the file list carries none.
6. Commit trailers: the model-free pair on all five non-merge commits.
7. The sentinel-owner case (a package-less runtime object's owner; a `?package=Q` save answered success with rows `[null, Q]`): the same D9.9 disagreement, deliberately excluded here because the prescription would name `'sys_metadata'` as a package and the remedy wording is a decision. Escalated to the D9.9 family's close-out, #23291, comment `6171964742`. Not a reason to hold this PR: the card's scope, a runtime owner bound to a package, is complete.
8. `duplicatePackage`'s prescription misfit (a same-name copy is told to bind to P or extend; renaming is the remedy there): filed as #23511. This PR's change on that face is not worse (①.3).
9. The prescription's second remedy names a code-package affordance (`objectExtensions`): noted; the ruled D9.9 text is reused unchanged and the first remedy is always available. Carrier: the D9.9 family's close-out, with 7.
10. The heal comment in `restoreArtifactRegistryView` stays true of stored rows: no action.

Check-runs on the head, read at 2026-10-14T15:44Z: 30 success, 6 skipped (the main-only battery and the opt-in smoke), 3 `in_progress`: `Test Core (2/6)`, `Test Core (3/6)`, `Test Core (4/6)`. Of the required contexts, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are success; `Test Core` is not yet complete. The landing waits for those three shards; the verdict below is on the contract face and does not stand in for them.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-23416-runtime-owner-overlay-refusal`
Reviewed-by: `session_0121ooBYRmS8ziFXm9ai5YHm`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对

`domain:spec` seat 4 (#18917) · `sunhaolin` · session `session_0121ooBYRmS8ziFXm9ai5YHm` · claim `6168029604` on #23416 · reviewed head `55bb8619e73ad18a8a08a776e7bdee92bca25d03` · 2026-10-14T15:51Z

**Verdict: ACCEPT.** Not governed (`check-governed-merges --pr 23510`), 5 files, +359 / −23. The `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review on this head is a PASS (`6172375603`). It lands after the landing clauses in item 6.

1. **Shape.**
   - The PR is a draft. Its first line is `Fixes #23416`, and `Clause-②: no` sits at line start.
   - The changeset makes `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` `minor` and marks it BREAKING with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`.
   - Its ADR-0087 marker reads `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, and the gate passes at the head.
   - FROM … TO … bullets cover the publish save, the draft save, `duplicatePackage` and the boot log line.
2. **Premises against the dispatch.**
   - The seat's ruling premise held. The registry keeps one own contributor per object name: `getObjectOwner(fqn)` reads `objectContributors.get(fqn)`, under the key `registerObject` uses (`computeFQN` is identity; both hydration seams pass no namespace).
   - The new arm predicts the registry's own ADR-0029 D3 refusal exactly. It reuses the existing D9.9 mismatch refusal (`422 OBJECT_OVERLAY_PACKAGE_MISMATCH`), with no new code and no new text.
   - The exclusions are right: the `'sys_metadata'` sentinel owner, an empty binding (re-addressed upstream by `packagelessAddress`), the owner's own package, and an owner with no `packageId`.
3. **Gates and evidence.**
   - Head check-runs at this record: 31 success, 6 skipped, 2 in progress (`Test Core (3/6)` and `(4/6)`), 0 failures.
   - The dev's local reconciliation ran 67 of 67 derived families.
   - The suites are green: metadata-protocol 236 files / 28397 tests, objectql 416 / 8097, rest 283 / 5852.
   - The new real-kernel pin went 2F/2P at base. Ablation A went 1F, as predicted, and the restore was proven.
   - The two re-seeded fixtures were each ablated against what they pin: B went 5F, D went 3F.
4. **Accepted deviations.**
   - Surface increment: the rest fixture from PR #23464, which landed after the claim, was re-seeded rather than weakened.
   - The classifier has three callers, not the two the dispatch assumed. None needed an edit.
   - The FROM → TO section label became bullets, per the gate's label convention.
   - `origin/main` was merged twice; the net diff is the five files.
5. **Out-of-scope dispositions.**
   - The sentinel-owner case (a package-less runtime object saved into a second package answers 200) is #23291's shape for objects. It was pointed there (`6171964742`), with no card.
   - The `duplicatePackage` prescription misfit for a non-prefixed object is filed as #23511. This PR moves it from a phantom `copied` to a reported `failed[]`, which is not worse.
   - The D9.9 second remedy naming a code-package affordance, and the heal comment, are Acceptance notes with `carrier:` none.
6. **Landing clauses.**
   - (a) The `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` PASS on the landing head: met (`6172375603`).
   - (b) Every check green or skipped by design: waits on `Test Core (3/6)` and `(4/6)`.
   - (c) `mergeable_state` clean at enqueue.
